speaker: Unknown
en: There's no computing problem that's ever been invented that doesn't utilize and can't utilize the microprocessor.
zh: 从来没有一个被发明出来的计算问题是不利用、也无法利用微处理器的。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is the heart of everything.
zh: 它是一切的心脏。

speaker: Unknown
en: All roads lead through it, around it, past it.
zh: 条条大路都穿过它、绕过它、经过它。

speaker: Unknown
en: Something has to do the orchestration, arbitration, decision around where those tokens go.
zh: 总得有什么东西来负责编排、仲裁、决定这些 token 去哪里。

speaker: Unknown
en: That's what CPUs do.
zh: 这就是 CPU 所做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Chip design can take anywhere from 24 to 36 months, depending on the complexity of the chip, et cetera, et cetera.
zh: 芯片设计可能需要 24 到 36 个月不等，取决于芯片的复杂度，等等，等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: The actual design is not the largest amount of time.
zh: 实际的设计并不是占用时间最多的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: The largest amount of time is in the verification, the validation, the debug.
zh: 占用时间最多的是验证、确认、调试。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI is really good at that.
zh: AI 非常擅长做这个。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if we were to shut it off, it's like being in the 1990s.
zh: 如果我们把它关掉，就像回到 1990 年代。

speaker: Unknown
en: You've got internet and you're now saying, you know, only internet between the hours of two and four.
zh: 你已经有了互联网，然后你现在说，你知道的，只有两点到四点之间提供互联网。

speaker: Unknown
en: After that, go to the library that we have down the hall.
zh: 之后，去走廊尽头我们设的那个图书馆。

speaker: Unknown
en: It'd be anarchy.
zh: 那会是无政府状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: The genie's out of the bottle and there's no stopping that.
zh: 精灵已经出了瓶子，没有什么能阻止这一点。

speaker: Unknown
en: Hi, listeners.
zh: 嗨，听众们。

speaker: Unknown
en: Welcome back to KnowPriors.
zh: 欢迎回到 KnowPriors。

speaker: Unknown
en: Today, Elad and I are here with Rene Haas, the CEO of Arm and SoftBank Group International.
zh: 今天，Elad 和我与 Rene Haas 在一起，他是 Arm 和 SoftBank Group International 的 CEO。

speaker: Unknown
en: We talk about the position of Arm within the chip industry, the resurgence of interest in chip innovation, the challenges of the supply chain, the future of robotics, energy, his place in the SoftBank Group, and how he sees workloads changing in the future and for Arm.
zh: 我们谈论了 Arm 在芯片行业中的地位、对芯片创新兴趣的复苏、供应链的挑战、机器人技术的未来、能源、他在软银集团中的位置，以及他如何看待未来工作负载的变化及其对 Arm 的意义。

speaker: Unknown
en: Rene, thanks so much for doing this with us.
zh: Rene,非常感谢你和我们一起做这期节目。

speaker: Unknown
en: Pleasure.
zh: 我的荣幸。

speaker: Unknown
en: Congratulations on the chip presentation on hot chips and all of the progress that Arm has made.
zh: 祝贺你在 Hot Chips 上的芯片展示，以及 Arm 取得的所有进展。

speaker: Unknown
en: I think there's an enormous amount of interest from the technology industry and the software industry in better understanding the chip supply chain recently.
zh: 我认为最近科技行业和软件行业对更好地理解芯片供应链有极大的兴趣。

speaker: Unknown
en: For anybody who's not super familiar, can you explain Arm's position in it?
zh: 对于那些不太熟悉的人，你能解释一下 Arm 在其中的位置吗？

speaker: Unknown
en: And then we'll get into more recent topics.
zh: 然后我们再进入更近期的话题。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have two positions in the chip supply chain.
zh: 我们在芯片供应链中有两个位置。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our primary business is licensing IP, the CPU core that finds its way into smartphones, data centers, automobiles, you name it.
zh: 我们的主要业务是授权 IP,也就是那些进入智能手机、数据中心、汽车等等的 CPU 核心。

speaker: Unknown
en: Our customers are the ones who either build the chips themselves, a Samsung who's got their own fab, or the vast majority of companies that take their chip designs and go to TSMC and get them taped out.
zh: 我们的客户要么自己制造芯片，比如拥有自己晶圆厂的 Samsung,要么是绝大多数公司，他们把芯片设计拿去 TSMC 进行流片。

speaker: Unknown
en: So in that world, and this is the cool thing about Arm,
zh: 所以在那个世界里，而这是 Arm 很酷的地方，

speaker: Unknown
en: Because we're so broad in terms of the markets that we serve, we kind of see everything.
zh: 因为我们所服务的市场非常广泛，我们几乎能看到一切。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a very good sense of what's going on in automotive, data center, smartphones.
zh: 我们对汽车、数据中心、智能手机领域正在发生的事情有非常清晰的了解。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we see the supply chain situation from all angles.
zh: 所以我们从各个角度看到供应链的情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: We also introduced our first product last March, the one you just mentioned at Hotchips, the Army GI CPU.
zh: 我们还在去年三月推出了我们的第一款产品，就是你刚才在 Hotchips 上提到的那个，Army GI CPU。

speaker: Unknown
en: So now we're in that soup ourselves from the standpoint of we're also having to figure out how to buy substrates and buy wafers and buy memory, et cetera, et cetera.
zh: 所以现在我们自己也在这个局里了，从我们也不得不琢磨怎么购买基板、购买晶圆、购买内存，等等等等的角度来看。

speaker: Unknown
en: We're up to our waist and everything on the supply side.
zh: 在供应侧的方方面面，我们都已经深陷到腰部了。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why'd you make the move now?
zh: 你们为什么现在走出这一步？

speaker: Unknown
en: ARM, I believe, existed for a few decades now.
zh: ARM,我记得，已经存在几十年了。

speaker: Unknown
en: The focus was always on IP, which is effectively designing the way that different chip components are put together, and then you license that out to other people to actually manufacture and incorporate into their designs.
zh: 重点一直放在 IP 上，也就是实际上设计不同芯片组件组合在一起的方式，然后把这个授权给别人去实际制造并整合到他们的设计中。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why did you decide to start making some of your own CPUs?
zh: 你们为什么决定开始制造一些自己的 CPU?

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, it was an evolution from the early days of where we just supplied simply the IP components, the pieces, the CPU IP, the GPU IP, the system IP, etc., etc.
zh: 是的，这是从早期的一个演变，那时我们只是简单供应 IP 组件、零件、CPU IP、GPU IP、系统 IP 等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: A few years ago, what we were starting to see was that product cycle times aren't slowing down.
zh: 几年前，我们开始看到的是产品周期时间并没有放慢。

speaker: Unknown
en: Chip manufacturing times are extending.
zh: 芯片制造时间在延长。

speaker: Unknown
en: The ability to get solutions out faster was becoming more and more important.
zh: 更快推出解决方案的能力变得越来越重要。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we moved from these individual components into what we called compute subsystems.
zh: 所以我们从这些单独的组件转向了我们所说的计算子系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: I used, when we did the roadshow a few years ago, I used the Lego analogy where essentially we're providing the blueprint on here's how you stitch it all together.
zh: 我在几年前做路演时，用了乐高的类比，本质上是我们提供蓝图，告诉你如何把所有东西拼接在一起。

speaker: Unknown
en: Demand for that was insane.
zh: 对此的需求是疯狂的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And what we were finding was, and we initially, people thought, well, people aren't going to want these subsystems because that's what a chip designer does.
zh: 而我们发现的是——而且最初，人们以为，嗯，人们不会想要这些子系统，因为那是芯片设计师做的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: Why are you providing that piece?
zh: 你们为什么要提供那个部分？

speaker: Unknown
en: But it saved time to market, and it saved a whole lot of things in terms of cost, speed, et cetera, et cetera.
zh: 但它节省了上市时间，在成本、速度，等等等等方面也节省了很多东西。

speaker: Unknown
en: The physical product was sort of the next leap, if you will.
zh: 实体产品可以说是下一个飞跃。

speaker: Unknown
en: And there are certain sets of customers that will license IP too, and they've got all the capability in the world to build chips based on ARM.
zh: 也有一类客户会选择授权 IP,他们拥有构建基于 ARM 的芯片的全部能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's a lot of companies who want to have product based on ARM.
zh: 有很多公司想要拥有基于 ARM 的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: Not all of our customers build products that serve those markets.
zh: 并非我们所有的客户都在构建服务于那些市场的产品。

speaker: Unknown
en: So Meta was that first example.
zh: 所以 Meta 是第一个例子。

speaker: Unknown
en: They wanted a general-purpose, agentic CPU.
zh: 他们想要一款通用的、面向智能体的 CPU。

speaker: Unknown
en: There wasn't anybody out who could give it to them.
zh: 当时没有任何人能够把这个提供给他们。

speaker: Unknown
en: They came to us and said, hey, why don't we do this together?
zh: 他们来找我们说，嘿，我们为什么不一起做这个呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's how we got into it.
zh: 我们就是这样进入这个领域的。

speaker: Unknown
en: How has that landed with the rest of your customer base?
zh: 这在你们其余的客户群体中反响如何？

speaker: Unknown
en: So one of the things that we were very careful about was getting, making sure the ecosystem was on board with this because we do CPU IP, which is really only as good as the ecosystem.
zh: 所以我们非常谨慎的事情之一，就是确保生态系统对此表示支持，因为我们做的是 CPU IP,而这实际上完全取决于生态系统的好坏。

speaker: Unknown
en: The ecosystem of chip people and the ecosystem of software folks and people who build around that.
zh: 芯片人才的生态系统、软件人才的生态系统，以及围绕这些进行构建的人的生态系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we talked to just about everybody who were customers and said, you know, how do you feel about this as direction we're going?
zh: 所以我们几乎和每一位客户都谈过，问他们，你们对我们走这个方向感觉如何？

speaker: Unknown
en: And surprisingly, we got a lot less pushback than I thought.
zh: 而出人意料的是，我们得到的反对比我预想的少得多。

speaker: Unknown
en: And the reason for that was the more software that's available in the wild, whether it's proprietary and or open source,
zh: 而原因是，市面上可用的软件越多，无论是专有的和/或开源的，

speaker: Unknown
en: Benefits the broader ecosystem and the customers themselves.
zh: 就会使更广泛的生态系统和客户自身受益。

speaker: Unknown
en: So whether it was NVIDIA, Amazon, Microsoft, Google, all people who build ARM-based server chips, they were all on board.
zh: 所以无论是 NVIDIA、Amazon、Microsoft、Google,这些构建基于 ARM 的服务器芯片的公司，他们全都表示支持。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think the ultimate proof point was when we announced the product last March, we had Jensen, we had Ronnie Boecker, we had Amin, we had James Hamilton, you know, all the folks from those customers I mentioned, all saying, congratulations, it's a great thing.
zh: 而我认为最终的证明是，当我们去年三月发布这款产品时，我们有 Jensen,有 Ronnie Boecker,有 Amin,有 James Hamilton,你懂的，所有来自我提到的那些客户的人，都在说，恭喜，这是一件很棒的事。

speaker: Unknown
en: So it's been okay.
zh: 所以情况还算不错。

speaker: Unknown
en: What is the, you know, where are you in the learning cycle as a business now selling physical chips that feels like a lot of new capabilities?
zh: 那么，你懂的，作为一家如今正在销售实体芯片的企业，你们在学习周期中处于什么位置？这感觉像是需要很多新能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, so we, obviously to deliver a product, and we're a fabless semi-company, right?
zh: 是的，所以我们要，显然要交付一款产品，而我们是一家无晶圆厂的半导体公司，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: We don't have a fab and we have no intention to build a fab, but we fit in that ecosystem.
zh: 我们没有晶圆厂，也没有打算建晶圆厂，但我们融入了那个生态系统。

speaker: Unknown
en: But that means you need supply chain operations people, you need to work with, as I said, the TSMCs and Samsungs of the world.
zh: 但这意味着你需要供应链运营人员，你需要与，正如我所说的，业界那些台积电和三星们合作。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need to work with the Samsungs and the Microns, the SK Hynix to get memory allocation.
zh: 你需要与三星、美光、SK 海力士合作，以获得内存分配。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then on the engineering side, you need a lot more different capabilities.
zh: 然后在工程方面，你需要更多不同的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: You need backend people, layout people, implementation people, bring up labs, physical stuff, right?
zh: 你需要后端人员、版图人员、实现人员、bring-up 实验室、实体性的东西，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: We didn't have a lot of physical stuff, which was kind of the beauty of the business, the original business.
zh: 我们原本没有太多实体性的东西，这算是这门生意的美妙之处，原来那门生意。

speaker: Unknown
en: I remember discovering that Arm had a 98.5% gross margin.
zh: 我记得我发现了 Arm 有 98.5% 的毛利率。

speaker: Unknown
en: Yeah, kind of beautiful.
zh: 是啊，挺美的。

speaker: Unknown
en: I don't think I've seen that otherwise.
zh: 我在其他地方没见过这种情况。

speaker: Unknown
en: I came from NVIDIA before I came over here.
zh: 在来这里之前，我来自 NVIDIA。

speaker: Unknown
en: Most of my career was in the chip world.
zh: 我职业生涯的大部分时间都在芯片行业。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I remember coming to Arm in 2013 and thinking, no inventory, no RMA, no scrap.
zh: 我记得 2013 年来到 Arm 时心想，没有库存，没有 RMA,没有报废品。

speaker: Unknown
en: What's not to like?
zh: 有什么不喜欢的呢？

speaker: Unknown
en: So we had to add a lot of those capabilities.
zh: 所以我们不得不补充很多这样的能力。

speaker: Unknown
en: We have a lot of people on the leadership team.
zh: 我们领导团队中有很多成员。

speaker: Unknown
en: Who've come from that world?
zh: 他们来自那个世界？

speaker: Unknown
en: I've got execs from Broadcom, Qualcomm, NVIDIA.
zh: 我有来自博通、高通、NVIDIA 的高管。

speaker: Unknown
en: I work for NVIDIA.
zh: 我为 NVIDIA 工作。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we have the leadership that's done this before in other companies.
zh: 所以我们拥有的领导层曾在其他公司做过这些事情。

speaker: Unknown
en: So we've been able to build up that muscle pretty quick.
zh: 所以我们能够很快地建立起那种肌肉。

speaker: Unknown
en: How have you approached AI adoption?
zh: 你们是如何推进 AI 采用的？

speaker: Unknown
en: So, you know, we were speaking earlier that there's news from OpenAI Editor today about Jalapeno, a new chip that they designed.
zh: 所以，你懂的，我们之前说过，今天有来自 OpenAI Editor 的新闻，关于 Jalapeno,一款他们设计的新芯片。

speaker: Unknown
en: Their claim is it was a very fast time to market.
zh: 他们的说法是，上市时间非常快。

speaker: Unknown
en: And part of that was using AI tooling to sort of design chips faster.
zh: 而其中一部分是使用 AI 工具来更快地设计芯片。

speaker: Unknown
en: How much adoption have you seen there?
zh: 你们在那方面看到了多少采用？

speaker: Unknown
en: I know other companies have also talked about things like adopting formal verification at Amazon or other places for their Trinium chips.
zh: 我知道其他公司也谈过类似的事情，比如在 Amazon 或其他地方，为他们的 Trinium 芯片采用形式验证。

speaker: Unknown
en: So I think the chip world is starting to evolve in terms of AI usage.
zh: 所以我认为芯片行业在 AI 使用方面正开始演化。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I'm just curious about how you've done that at all.
zh: 我只是很好奇你们究竟是如何做到这一点的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Well, personally, I'm a huge believer in AI as a utility that's going to help productivity for every single industry.
zh: 嗯，就个人而言，我坚信 AI 是一种将帮助每一个行业提升生产力的公用事业。

speaker: Unknown
en: It is going to be the great leveler in terms of companies that get started super quickly.
zh: 它将成为伟大的平衡器，让公司能够极其迅速地起步。

speaker: Unknown
en: And for industries, whether it's healthcare, infrastructure, robotics,
zh: 而对于各个行业，无论是医疗保健、基础设施、机器人技术，

speaker: Unknown
en: Every industry is going to use artificial intelligence as a utility and stop.
zh: 每个行业都将把人工智能当作一种公用事业来使用，然后到此为止。

speaker: Unknown
en: So since I'm such a believer in this, of course, we use it very heavily inside of Arm.
zh: 所以既然我对此如此深信不疑，当然，我们在 Arm 内部也非常大量地使用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: On the non-engineering side, we're using it all over the place.
zh: 在非工程方面，我们到处都在使用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: But on the engineering side, we've seen huge, huge benefit.
zh: 但在工程方面，我们看到了巨大的、巨大的收益。

speaker: Unknown
en: You mentioned verification.
zh: 你提到了验证。

speaker: Unknown
en: Chip design can take anywhere from 24 to 36 months, depending on the complexity of the chip, et cetera, et cetera.
zh: 芯片设计可能需要24到36个月不等，取决于芯片的复杂程度等等，等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: The actual design of the architecture, the RTL generation, if you will, the mapping of the architecture
zh: 架构的实际设计、RTL 生成，可以这么说，架构的映射

speaker: Unknown
en: It's not the largest amount of time.
zh: 这并不是占用时间最多的部分。

speaker: Unknown
en: The largest amount of time is in the verification, the validation, the debug, the documentation, et cetera, et cetera.
zh: 占用时间最多的是验证、确认、调试、文档等等，等等。

speaker: Unknown
en: AI is really good at that.
zh: AI 非常擅长这些。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I would say we probably have 80 to 90% of engineers today in Sidearm who use it on a daily basis.
zh: 我想说的是，今天在 Sidearm 我们大概有80%到90%的工程师每天都在使用它。

speaker: Unknown
en: And if we were to shut it off, my analogy I give to people, it's like being in the 1990s, you've got internet and you're now saying, you know, only internet between the hours of two and four.
zh: 而如果我们要把它关掉，我给人们举的类比是，这就像身处1990年代，你已经有了互联网，现在你却说，你知道的，只能在两点到四点之间用互联网。

speaker: Unknown
en: After that, go to the library that we have down the hall that's got all the books that you can go up and look all this information up.
zh: 在那之后，就去走廊那头的图书馆，那里有所有的书，你可以走过去查找所有这些信息。

speaker: Unknown
en: People, it'd be anarchy.
zh: 大家，那会是无政府状态。

speaker: Unknown
en: So the genie's out of the bottle, right?
zh: 所以精灵已经从瓶子里出来了，对吧？

speaker: Unknown
en: And there's no stopping that.
zh: 而这是无法阻止的。

speaker: Unknown
en: Now, there's certain things that the tools are still not that mature of.
zh: 现在，在某些事情上，这些工具还不是很成熟。

speaker: Unknown
en: One of them is really around RTL generation and then physical design and implementation in best of class.
zh: 其中之一确实是围绕 RTL 生成，以及物理设计和实现方面的同类最佳水平。

speaker: Unknown
en: And that's simply because the models
zh: 而这仅仅是因为这些模型

speaker: Unknown
en: You know, they're trained on what's available publicly.
zh: 你知道的，它们是用公开可得的资料训练的。

speaker: Unknown
en: And a lot of the information is quite proprietary.
zh: 而很多信息是相当专有的。

speaker: Unknown
en: That being said, there's massive opportunity between the ecosystems and everyone in the industry to make that better.
zh: 话虽如此，在生态系统之间以及行业中的每个人之间，还有巨大的机会来把这方面做得更好。

speaker: Unknown
en: It's only going to get better.
zh: 它只会变得越来越好。

speaker: Unknown
en: Have you been fine-tuning models to try and address that gap, given the proprietary information that you offer us?
zh: 鉴于你们提供给我们的专有信息，你们有没有在微调模型来尝试解决那个差距？

speaker: Unknown
en: We've been working with model makers around that, absolutely.
zh: 我们一直在围绕这一点与模型厂商合作，绝对是。

speaker: Unknown
en: And I think that's a big, big opportunity.
zh: 我认为这是一个巨大的、巨大的机会。

speaker: Unknown
en: And one of the things that I'm proud of at Arm
zh: 而我在 Arm 感到自豪的事情之一

speaker: Unknown
en: Thank you for joining us.
zh: 感谢你们加入我们。

speaker: Unknown
en: That have said, hey, why don't we license this IP that we've got because it's really, really valuable.
zh: 那些说过，嘿，我们为什么不把我们拥有的这个 IP 授权出去，因为它真的真的很有价值。

speaker: Unknown
en: And then you get into, well, wait a minute, there's no documentation.
zh: 然后你就发现，嗯，等一下，没有文档。

speaker: Unknown
en: There's no explanation on how you- No one's ever gonna be able to use this.
zh: 没有解释你该如何——没有人能够使用这个。
